probe_finding: Definition (author @throwthedamball, read 2026-10-15): disruption pressure is pressure that arrives BEFORE the QB has completed his read — it breaks the play's timing; non-disruption pressure arrives after the read, when the QB has already had his chance to execute. ATTRIBUTED CLAIM (author's stated research claim, Dec 24 2025 post): disruption pressure is 'nearly 4x as punishing' to an offense as non-disruption pressure. Recorded as a claim with its date and author, never as a finding: if the engine ever uses the 4x figure, it uses it as the author's published estimate, attributed, until an in-house measurement exists. Role in-engine: it refines raw pressure rate (C-290/C-323 count and time pressures; this says WHEN in the read the pressure lands is the damaging part) — the timing distinction behind tonight's trench-cascade reasoning.

attributed_claim.claim: disruption pressure is nearly 4x as punishing to an offense as non-disruption pressure
